Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

graphlearnR 0.1.0

First release.

Graph data

  • graph_data() stores homogeneous graphs with 1-based edge_index, node and edge features, labels, weights, masks, and identifiers. Undirected input is given once per pair and stored in both directions with edge_pair.
  • Conversions with igraph, edge lists, and dense or sparse adjacency matrices; graph_tensors() moves a graph to torch tensors on any device.
  • graph_batch() and unbatch() combine graphs into one disconnected graph and back.
  • Transforms: self loops, coalescing, induced subgraphs, symmetrization, feature normalization, degree features.

Message passing and layers

  • cheb_conv() (ChebConv), pna_conv() with pna_degree() (PNA), appnp() and appnp_model() (APPNP), and sag_pool() (SAGPool).
  • Scatter aggregations (sum, mean, max, min, std, softmax) and message_passing() for custom layers.
  • Layers: GraphSAGE, GCN, GraphConv, GIN and GINE, GAT, GATv2, graph transformer convolution, edge conditioned convolution (NNConv), and RGCN with basis decomposition.
  • Global add, mean, max, and attention pooling, top-k pooling, and DiffPool (dense_diff_pool(), to_dense_adj(), dense_graph_conv(), diffpool_model()), whose auxiliary losses the trainer adds.
  • hgt_conv(): heterogeneous graph transformer layer, also available as hetero_gnn_model(conv = "hgt").
  • gnn_model() builds node, edge, link, and graph level models with normalization, residual connections, and dropout.

Training and evaluation

  • train_graph_model() trains node, edge, link, and graph classification and regression models, full batch or with neighbor sampling, with early stopping, schedulers, checkpoints, and a reproducibility record.
  • predict(), evaluate_graph_model(), save_graph_fit(), and load_graph_fit().
  • Leakage-safe splits for nodes, edges, edge labels, and graphs (random, stratified, group, scaffold).
  • Metrics for classification, calibration, regression, ranking, and clustering.

Sampling and scale

  • sample_neighbors(), k_hop_subgraph(), node and graph loaders, negative sampling, and corrupted tails for ranking evaluation.
  • cluster_loader() (Cluster-GCN) and saint_loader() (GraphSAINT random walks with loss and edge normalization), used through train_graph_model(loader = ).

Heterogeneous, temporal, and transformer models

  • hetero_graph_data(), reverse relations, typed sampling, typed link splits, hetero_conv(), and hetero_gnn_model().
  • Event based temporal graphs, snapshots, strictly causal temporal neighbors, a graph GRU, spatiotemporal forecasting, and dynamic link prediction with baselines.
  • tgn_model() and train_tgn(): temporal graph networks with node memory and time, graph sum, or graph attention embeddings.
  • hgt_conv(temporal_encoding = TRUE) and the edge_time field of heterogeneous relations add HGT’s relative temporal encoding.
  • graph_ode_block() and graph_ode_model(): GRAND style continuous depth diffusion with fixed step Runge-Kutta or Euler integration.
  • Laplacian and random walk positional encodings, shortest path distances, and a Graphormer style graph transformer.

Explainability

  • Saliency, integrated gradients, edge gradients, occlusion, GNNExplainer, attention weights, explanation subgraphs, fidelity, and stability.

Datasets

  • Built in: Zachary’s karate club, stochastic block models, and synthetic graph, heterogeneous, and temporal datasets.
  • Downloaders with checksum verification for TU datasets and the LINQS citation graphs (Cora, CiteSeer); nothing third party is bundled.
  • download_ogb(), read_ogb_node(), and read_ogb_graph() for OGB node and graph property datasets in their CSV layout, with official splits.

Molecules

  • molecule_graph() builds graphs from atoms and bonds with element and bond order features; dataset_synthetic_molecules() generates small synthetic molecules with scaffold identifiers for scaffold splits.

Models, evaluation and data (additions)

  • meta_layer() composes edge, node and graph level updates (graph network block, as PyG’s MetaLayer).
  • predict() for temporal fits: TGN continues from its stored memory and neighbor store, dynamic link models score from earlier snapshots, and spatiotemporal models forecast from given origins; temporal fits can be saved and loaded.
  • Heterogeneous node tasks train on typed neighbor samples with fanouts and batch_size.
  • ladies_loader(): layer wise importance sampled node batches (LADIES, the successor of FastGCN) for train_graph_model(loader = ).
  • evaluate_embeddings() (linear probe and clustering), average precision in classification metrics, filtered per positive link ranking in evaluate_graph_model(), and ogb_evaluate() with the official OGB metrics; the bce_masked loss trains multi task targets with missing labels.
  • Datasets check a shared feature schema (graph_schema()); download_pubmed_raw() and read_linqs_pubmed() read Pubmed-Diabetes.
  • igraph conversion keeps feature names, label matrices, edge masks, graph labels, graph attributes and metadata; unbatch() rebuilds heterogeneous batches.
  • The reproducibility record keeps exact split members and all training settings.
  • graph_transformer_model() caches shortest path distances of recent batches.
  • scatter_std() (and the PNA std aggregator) now returns 0 for empty and constant groups, as PyTorch Geometric’s StdAggregation; PNA layers are compared with PyG’s PNAConv in the benchmark workflow.

Correctness and safety behavior

  • split_edges() and split_edges_hetero() treat parallel duplicates (and, for undirected or same type relations, both orientations) as one unit, so a held out pair never stays in the training graph.
  • Masks are checked for pairwise overlap, including edge masks; train_spatiotemporal_model() purges windows that cross split boundaries.
  • Class labels share one level set across batches, splits and predictions; metrics check that truth and prediction lengths match.
  • TGN updates memory in event order, never draws the positive pair as a negative, keeps events with one timestamp in one batch, and checks that train, validation and test periods do not overlap.
  • Saved fits keep link decoders and heterogeneous link schemas; edge predictions for given pairs use the features of the matching edges.
  • Explainers restore the model’s training mode and parameter gradient flags; gnn_explainer() supports regression and rejects models that ignore edge weights.
  • Sub seeds are drawn with sample.int(), so seed arithmetic never overflows.
  • Training errors on mini batch options a task would ignore (fanouts, batch_size, loader), and write_graph_dataset() will not mix files with an existing dataset unless overwrite = TRUE.
  • Downloads without a recorded checksum warn; OGB archives use https.

Sibling packages (optional)

  • graph_diffusion() simulates diffusion on a graph with the modelcompR ODE solvers.
  • graph_operator_symbolic() returns exact adjacency, Laplacian, and GCN operators as symcompR matrices.
  • consistent_labels() finds the most probable labeling that obeys edge rules with the z3r optimizer.
  • select_links() chooses links under a budget as a 0-1 program in optcompR.
  • aggregate_jax() performs neighborhood aggregation with jaxR arrays.
  • luz_node_dataloader() and luz_node_module train node models with luz; augment() and glance() methods summarize fits for tidymodels.
